data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The resilience comparison is underspecified without bounding the dependency graph; decentralized networks are only more resilient when their internal coupling is strictly lower than the large service's internal coupling, and evidence distinguishing truly independent failures requires constructing a causal DAG (directed acyclic graph) of the system and performing conditional independence tests to determine whether observed failures are marginally independent or only conditionally independent given a latent variable.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the dependency graph cannot be fully characterized (e.g., due to unobservable external dependencies), then conditional independence tests may yield misleading results.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the large service's internal bulkheads are incomplete (e.g., shared state persists across cell boundaries), then its dependency graph is denser than assumed.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the decentralized network's nodes share more dependencies than the large service's internal subsystems, then the network is not more resilient despite its decentralization.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Resilience to correlated failure is not a function of scale or decentralization per se, but of the structure of the dependency graph. A decentralized network of small services may have high external coupling (shared cloud providers, shared libraries, shared upstream dependencies) that makes it vulnerable to correlated failures, while a large service may implement internal bulkheads that isolate failure domains. The key evidence to distinguish truly independent failures from hidden shared causes involves: (1) constructing a causal DAG of the system's dependencies (both internal and external), (2) collecting failure data across a representative time period, and (3) performing conditional independence tests: if failures are marginally independent, they are truly independent; if they are only conditionally independent given some latent variable, a shared cause exists.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
